Androgeos is the same person as Androgeus, so this duplicates the Androgeus link; the form should be merged rather than kept as a second child.
Tecmessa was a captive concubine won in war, not a wife; under the editor's rule that only marriages count as spouse, she is read as a lover.
Hesione was given to Telamon as war prize after Heracles' sack of Troy (Ovid, Metamorphoses); a captive concubine, not a wife, so per editor rule only marriages count as spouse.
Harmonia was wife of Cadmus; Ares was only her father (Apollodorus 3.4.2) or lover; editor rule treats non-marriage as lover. Her parentage is stated by the book itself.
Duplicate of Penthesilea under a variant spelling; the same person, so the duplicate node should be merged.

link: Ares parent_of Melanippus, son of Ares
reasons: A garbled name label for a son of Ares; it is not a distinct character.
Ares and Theogone are the parents of Tmolus the mountain god (Ovid, Metamorphoses 11), while Apollodorus's Tmolus is the Lydian king, husband of Omphale; the Wikidata entry merges the two.
Ismenis is a daughter of Asopus and Metope; in Pausanias Caanthus is a son of Oceanus and Tethys, and Theoi lists no such child for him.

Menoitios son of Actor and Aegina is a different tradition from Apollodorus; in Apollodorus (1.9.16, 3.13.8) Menoetius is son of Actor and Aegina, so this is Menoetius the father of Patroclus, and the duplicate entry should be merged or removed.
Pausanias' Anticlea at Pharae, daughter of Diocles and wife of Machaon, is a different woman from Odysseus' mother Anticlea, daughter of Autolycus.
Pasithea is a Grace, not Hera's child; Hera only promises her to Hypnos in the Iliad, and Theoi lists no such parentage.
Hesiod does not make Aidos a child of Prometheus; Aidos (Shame) is a personification with no ancestry here, a misread of the Theoi listing.
The Iliad never mentions Alpheus pursuing Artemis; the story is a local Pausanias tale (Alpheus and Arethusa/Artemis Alpheiaia in Elis), a cult legend and not part of Homer's account.

Athamas is son of Aeolus (Apollodorus, Pausanias); Minyas is not his father. Wikidata likely confuses with Orchomenus/Athamas lore; Pausanias makes Orchomenus his son and says nothing of Athamas as his son.
Athamas is normally the son of Aeolus (Apollodorus, Theoi); Minyas is a Wikidata confusion. Pausanias does not make Minyas his father.
Hyperion is a Titan; Pausanias does not make him Agamemnon's child. Likely a misread, since Agamemnon's children are Orestes, Iphigenia, Electra, Chrysothemis and others (Hyperion is not among them).
Anaxibia is Agamemnon's sister (daughter of Atreus, wife of Strophius) in Pausanias, not his daughter.
Iole's father is Eurytus of Oechalia, the archer. Pindar's Eurytos is the Argonaut son of Hermes, so the link belongs to the other man.
Iphitus is the son of Eurytus of Oechalia (Odyssey, Apollodorus), not of Hermes' son the Argonaut.
Antioche is the wife of Hermes' son Eurytus in Hesiod's tradition and belongs to the Oechalian family or another figure, not to Pindar's Argonaut.
Thalpius son of Eurytus is the Epeian (Actorione) of the Iliad, a different Eurytus.
Pausanias' Eurytus, husband of Theraphone, is the Actorione, not Hermes' son in Pindar.

Apollodorus (Epitome 1.4) calls Sinis son of Polypemon and Sylea, but this Polypemon is the father of Sinis, not Procrustes; Polypemon is only a name of Procrustes elsewhere (Damastes), so the link confuses two beings.
Amalthea is the nurse of Zeus (a goat or nymph), not a child of Helios; likely a confusion with another figure.
In Statius' Thebaid, Argus is the Argive king, father of Deipyle and Argia (Adrastus's line), not the Argonaut son of Phrixus; the link belongs to the shipbuilder Argus of the Argonautica.
Chalciope's son Argus is the Argonautica figure who sailed with the Argonauts; he is not Statius' Argus, the Argive ancestor.
Adrastus was king of Argos and Polynices' father-in-law, not his son; Pausanias gives Thersander as the son of Polynices and Argia, and Adrastus's descendants are separate.
Metamorphoses and Homer (Iliad) give Panthous as Euphorbus' father; Alcimachus is unsupported for him and likely a confusion with another figure.

Schoeneus is usually son of Athamas only in some Boeotian traditions, but more commonly of Athamas via Themisto? Not in Pausanias or Theoi's main listing; Schoeneus is the father of Atalanta in Boeotian accounts, so this is a doubtful link.

Apollodorus gives Meleager a child only by Atalanta (Parthenopaeus is sometimes so named); Polydora is Pausanias' tradition of a daughter, but Apollodorus (1.8.3) says Meleager married Cleopatra and has Polydora only as Protesilaus' wife in other traditions, so the link is unsupported in this book.
Anchises' father is Capys (Iliad 20.239: Dardanus, Erichthonius, Tros, Assaracus, Capys, Anchises); Dardanus is a remote ancestor, not his father.
This is Io, daughter of Inachus, confused with the Egyptian goddess Isis. In Pausanias Isis is the Egyptian goddess, though he mentions Io's identification with her in Egypt.
Zeus's lover was Io, not the Egyptian goddess Isis; the other books' link belongs to Io.
Peiren is a father of Io in Hesiod's tradition (Io as Isis), not of the Egyptian goddess.
Leosthenes, the Athenian general of the Lamian War, was the son of an earlier Leosthenes (exiled 362/1 BC), not of any Hippocrates.
Editor ruled Jove as parent of Pasithea wrong everywhere; Pasithea is a Grace in Iliad 14 given to Hypnos, and Hera is not her mother in the tradition (Pausanias gives Aegle).
Pausanias' Troilus, son of Alcinous, is a different figure; the Odyssey names Alcinous' sons as Laodamas, Halius and Clytoneus, and no Troilus is among them.
Pausanias' Alcetus, son of Alcinous, is a different figure; the Odyssey names Alcinous' sons as Laodamas, Halius and Clytoneus, and no Alcetus is among them.

link: Ares parent_of Melanippus, son of Ares
reasons: This is a garbled node name from Pausanias; the Melanippus is a different Theban figure, not a clear son of Ares.
Hermes is a son of Zeus and Maia, so a half-brother, not a full sibling; the sibling link is loose but not contradicted, however Statius uses it figuratively.
Penthesileia duplicates Penthesilea, the same Amazon under a variant spelling; merge the two names.

link: Eurydice spouse_of Philip of Macedon, son of Amyntas
reasons: Pausanias calls Eurydice, daughter of Antipater, wife of Philip (a different Eurydice from Ptolemy's wife); the Philip link belongs to Philip's Eurydice, the Ptolemy link is right for Antipater's daughter.
Nestor's wife Eurydice in the Odyssey tradition is a different person, not Ptolemy's wife.
Pausanias: this Eurydice, daughter of Lacedaemon, is the wife of Acrisius, not Ptolemy's wife.
Acrisius' wife Eurydice is the daughter of Lacedaemon, a distinct person from Ptolemy's wife.
Orpheus' wife Eurydice is the mythic figure, unrelated to Ptolemy's wife.
Editor ruled Zeus-Selene links wrong; Selene (Moon) mixed with other Selene/Luna figures.
Editor decision: Zeus parent of Selene is wrong everywhere.
Pandia is tied to Selene; the Zeus-Selene link is ruled wrong, so this one rests on a namesake mix-up.
Pandora was made by Hephaestus; Zeus was not her lover. Hesiod's Pandora daughter of Deucalion is a different being.
A group taken for a person; Nymphs and Naiads are not a single child.
A group taken for a person.
A group node duplicates the individual Muses already listed.
A group node duplicates Aglaea, Euphrosyne and Thalia.
Editor says Sibyl's parents are Lamia or Theodorus (Pausanias), not Zeus.
Editor decision.
Personification without a firm tradition; unsupported.
Unsupported guess for a personification.
Personification, unsupported.
Pallas is a Titan or giant, or an epithet of Athena, not Zeus's child.
Editor: Midas parent of Xanthus only in Hesiod; no Zeus link.
Hermus is a river, not Zeus's son.
Eetion father of Andromache is mortal, no Zeus parentage.
Hesiod makes Eris daughter of Night.
Hecate is daughter of Perses and Asteria.
Nemesis is daughter of Night, or Oceanus in some accounts; not Zeus.
Sisyphus is son of Aeolus.
Macar is son of Aeolus or Helios in tradition.
Apollodorus gives Pelasgus as a son of Zeus and Niobe, so keep it only through that tradition.
Cybele is conflated with Rhea or Ops, who is the mother.

Theoi lists Okeanos and Tethys as parents of the Oceanids, but Nephele is not among them. Wikidata's Oceanus link belongs to the Ixion cloud-figure or is an unsupported guess, and this book gives Nephele no parents.

Callirrhoe and Callirhoe are duplicate spellings of one name, and the daughter of Acheloüs (wife of Alcmaeon) is a different person from the Oceanid Callirhoe; the duplicate link should be merged into one.

Pausanias's sentence is cut off and says Dysponteus was the son of Œnomaus only as a Pisan/Dyspontii tradition; the text is not confirmed here as Œnomaus's own story, and Dysponteus is a founder figure of the Dyspontii. Actually the book states he was 'they state the son' of Œnomaus, so this is a book tradition.
Glaucon is not a son of Eteocles in Apollodorus; Pausanias mentions a Glaucus as son of Sisyphus or Eteocles' line only in a different context, and Apollodorus names Laodamas as Eteocles' son.
Metamorphoses' Midas is the Phrygian king, son of Gordius and Cybele; Cybele was identified with Rhea but not in Pindar, and the link is not part of Rhea's Olympian family.
Charillus son of Polydectes is the Spartan king, whose father Polydectes was a Eurypontid king of Sparta, not the Seriphian king.
Eunomus father of the Spartan Polydectes (Pausanias) is a different man; Seriphian Polydectes is son of Magnes (or Peristhenes/Poseidon) and Cerebia.
Athamas was a son of Aeolus, not of Minyas; the link confuses two figures (Athamas of Boeotia and Minyas of Orchomenus).
Athamas is the son of Aeolus (Apollodorus, Hesiod); Minyas is confused with him, though Minyas is a different figure, an Orchomenian king, and not Athamas's father.
This is a group node for Alcithoë and her sisters, not a separate person; the individual daughter links already cover it.
Deidameia bore Neoptolemus to Achilles on Scyros; the book gives no marriage, so per the editor's rule it is a lover.

Metamorphoses 2 only says Nyctimene defiled her father's bed and never names him; Theoi/Hyginus (Fab. 204) give Epopeus of Lesbos as the father, while Nycteus is Antiope's father in Thebes, so the link confuses two traditions.
Hesione as his wife comes from Aeschylus. Hesiod's Catalogue gives Pronoea as the mother of Deucalion, and the Theogony names no wife for Prometheus.
Aetnaeus comes from a Pausanias local tradition (Sicilian Aetna), not from Hesiod, and the Hesiod text does not support it.
Aidos as a child of Prometheus is a late or obscure tradition. Hesiod does not say so, and in his poems Aidos is not Prometheus's child.
Pausanias' Chthonia, sister of Clymenus son of Phoroneus at Hermione, is a different person; the cult title Chthonia was merged into Demeter, so the sibling link is wrong.

Procris, wife of Cephalus, is not Arcesius's mother in the tradition. Ovid's Ulysses names only Jupiter as Arcesius's father, and in Ovid Procris's marriage to Cephalus is childless. The Wikidata mother is a confusion with another Cephalus line.

Arcesius is the father of Laertes, son of Zeus or Cephalus in some accounts; Procris is not his mother. Ancient sources (Ovid, Apollodorus) have Procris childless, and Cephalus is sometimes named as Arcesius' father by Hyginus, not Procris.
Scylla the monster is not Triton's daughter in the Aeneid; the Argonautica link doesn't carry over to this book's Triton, and Theoi's confirmation rests on a rare variant.
Tecmessa was a captive concubine won in war, not a wife; the editor's rule reads non-marriage spouse links as lovers.

Apollodorus (Library 2.5.4) calls Pholus the son of Silenus and a Melian nymph, but he is a centaur. Theoi lists this as a variant, though the link confuses the centaur Pholus with a satyr family; in Ovid's Metamorphoses Pholus is a centaur with no tie to Silenus.
The quoted sentence is about Eurytus son of Actor and Molione, one of the Moliones, not Eurytus of Oechalia, who is the father of Iole and Iphitus.
Pausanias' Theraphone, mother of Thalpius, belongs to the Eurytus son of Actor (Molione's line), not to Eurytus of Oechalia.
Thalpius is the son of Eurytus son of Actor, one of the Moliones, not of Eurytus of Oechalia.
Hesiod's Antioche is the wife of Eurytus of Oechalia, but the tradition is unclear. Given the namesake confusion and the editor's rule, the spouse link is unsupported in this book.
Leocritus is the son of Arisbas in the Odyssey and Iliad (Leocritus son of Euenor is a suitor in the Odyssey); Pausanias does not make him Polydamas's son, and the link seems to confuse namesakes.

Apollodorus 3.12.2 gives the Trojan Erichthonius, son of Dardanus, who fathered Tros. The Athenian Erichthonius, son of Hephaestus, is a different being. Dardanus, Tros and Astyoche belong to the Trojan one.
Tros is the son of the Trojan Erichthonius (Apollodorus 3.12.2), not of the Athenian king.
Perses the Titan is son of Crius and Eurybia. Helios's son Perses (brother of Aeetes) is a different figure with the same name.
Pausanias says Araethyrea was Phlias's mother and not Chthonophyle, who was his wife.
Pausanias says Phlias was Chthonophyle's husband, not her son; his mother was Aræthyrea.

The editor's rule is that only marriages count as spouse. Callidice is a Thesprotian queen whom the Telegony summary says he married, but the flagged spouse link is treated as a lover, not a wife, since Penelope is the wife.
This Phoebe is the Messenian daughter of Leucippus; Earth (Gaia) is the mother of the Titaness Phoebe, who is a different being. Pausanias' link belongs to the Titan.
Opheltes (Archemorus) is the son of Lycurgus of Nemea, king of Nemea, not the Thracian Lycurgus of Iliad 6.
Iasus is a child of Arcadian Lycurgus, son of Aleus; Apollodorus's Arcadian Lycurgus is not the Thracian king.
Amphidamas is a son of Arcadian Lycurgus, son of Aleus, so belongs to the other Lycurgus.
Agathinus, son of Thrasybulus, is honored by the Achaeans of Pellene, so he is not the Athenian general's son and most likely belongs to another Thrasybulus.
Hesiod makes Theia the wife of Hyperion and sister of Oceanus; she is not his wife, and Tethys is his only marriage.
The Xanthus of the Trojan river is a river god and a son of Oceanus, but the Xanthus linked in other books is the horse or the Lycian figure; this link confuses namesakes.
Hesione the Oceanid wife of Prometheus is in Aeschylus, but Hesione daughter of Laomedon is the other Hesione; the link takes the wrong one.
Passalus was one of the Cercopes, not a child of Oceanus; the link is unsupported.
Apollodorus 3.3.1 names a different Deucalion, son of Minos and father of Idomeneus, Crete and Molus, not the son of Prometheus.
Apollodorus 3.3.1 gives Molus to Deucalion son of Minos, not the flood hero.
Deidameia bore Neoptolemos to Achilles on Skyros, but no source calls this a marriage; under the editor's rule it is a lover link.
The union with Helen on Leuke is an afterlife tradition (Pausanias) and not a marriage, so it is read as a lover link under the editor's rule.
The Achilles and Helen union on the White Island is a late tale of an afterlife pairing (Pausanias), not a marriage.

link: Achilles parent_of Pyrrhus, king of Epirus
reasons: Pyrrhus, king of Epirus, is the later historical king and not the son of Achilles. Pyrrhus is the mythical son's other name, Neoptolemos, which is already linked, so this is a duplicate.
Pausanias' Pisus (founder of Pisa in Elis) is not a son of Messenian Perieres in the usual tradition; Hesiod's Perieres has Aphareus and Leucippus, so this looks like a confusion.
Hesiod makes Aegle a woman Theseus loved (he abandoned Ariadne for her); no marriage is attested.
Hippolyta/Antiope the Amazon is Theseus' captive partner and mother of Hippolytus; Statius treats her as wife, but only marriages count and the same figure is Antiope.
The book spells Demophon as Demophoon; this duplicates the Demophon link, so one person has two entries.

Callidice, queen of the Thesprotians, is a tradition from the Telegony (Odysseus's marriage to her after his wanderings); she is not his wife in Pausanias, and under the editor's rule any non-marriage spouse link is read as a lover.
Editor's rule reads any spouse link other than the listed marriages as a lover; Pausanias says Boreas 'married' her, but the editor's decision is final, so it is recorded as a lover link.
Hermione is a variant name for Harmonia (Ovid sometimes), so this duplicates the Harmonia marriage; or confuses Menelaus' daughter Hermione with Harmonia. Cadmus's only wife is Harmonia.
Pausanias' Electra is a Theban gate-name/Atlas's daughter Electra, mother of Harmonia/Iasion in some accounts, not Agenor's child; Cadmus's sister is Europa.
Vesta's mother is Ops (Rhea), Saturn's wife. Cybele is a distinct Phrygian goddess, though sometimes syncretized with Ops/Rhea; Metamorphoses does not make her Vesta's mother.
Passalus is one of the Cercopes; in Hesiod's tradition and elsewhere he is not a child of Theia, so this link was misattached from another book.
Theia's husband is Hyperion (Hesiod, Theogony); Oceanus is the husband of Tethys, so this confuses the two Titan sisters.
Epicasta as Nestor's daughter appears only in Hesiod's tradition (mother of Homer), which the editor limits to Hesiod; Pausanias does not tell it.
Selene (Moon) is not Apollo's sister; Artemis is. The editor rules Selene links wrong; Ovid's Diana/Moon identification is not a sibling link for Selene.
Scylla is usually the daughter of Phorcys or Crataeis; the Apollo parentage rests on a rare Hesiodic fragment and is unsupported by Theoi.
Hilaeira was a daughter of Leucippus, not Apollo; this confuses her with a namesake.
Hymenaeus is more usually a son of Apollo, not a lover; the lover link is unsupported.
Ileus (Locrian Oileus) is not a known lover of Apollo; the fragment is dubious.
This is Cleopatra I of Egypt, mother of Ptolemy Philometor, not Idas' daughter, the wife of Meleager.

link: Cleopatra parent_of Alexander, son of Cleopatra
reasons: This is the Ptolemaic queen Cleopatra, mother of Alexander (Ptolemy X), not the mythic Cleopatra.

link: Philip of Macedon, son of Amyntas parent_of Cleopatra
reasons: Pausanias' Cleopatra daughter of Philip II is the historical Macedonian princess, sister of Alexander the Great, not Meleager's wife.
Pausanias' Pandion is the Athenian king; Oeneus the Calydonian is son of Porthaon, as the Hesiod fragment says. Likely a namesake confusion with Oeneus son of Pandion of Athens.
Mothone is the daughter of the Athenian Oeneus in Pausanias, not the Calydonian Oeneus.
Pausanias (9.5.10-11) follows the Oedipodea: Euryganeia, daughter of Hyperphas, was Oedipus's wife and mother of his four children. Wikidata lists her as a spouse, so lover is wrong.
This is a group node that duplicates the individual sons Polynices and Eteocles, who are already linked.
Charillus is the Spartan king of Pausanias, son of Polydectes of Sparta (Eunomid line), not the Seriphian king of Metamorphoses.

link: Dexamenus parent_of Eurypylus, son of Euaemon
reasons: Pausanias says some writers claim the chest went to a different Eurypylus, son of Dexamenus and king at Olenus, who came with Heracles. The Thessalian Eurypylus is son of Euaemon, so this link belongs to the Olenus namesake.

link: Thetis parent_of Phocus, son of Æacus
reasons: Phocus son of Aeacus was born to Psamathe, a different Nereid, not Thetis; Thetis's son is Achilles by Peleus.
Endeis was the daughter of Chiron and wife of Aeacus, mother of Peleus; she is not Thetis's sister, since Thetis's parents are Nereus and Doris.
Aidos (Shame) is not a child of Prometheus in Hesiod or Theoi's listing; the link is a misreading, so it is unsupported in this tree.
Pausanias's Aetnaeus is a Sicilian epithet or cult figure linked to Zeus and Hephaestus, not a son of Prometheus; the link is an unsupported guess.

Clytius is a son of Alcmaeon only in Pausanias' tradition (via Alphesiboea/Arsinoe); Apollodorus never says this, but this is unsupported in this book, so merely unconfirmed, not contradicted.... treated as keep-level.
Duplicate of Callirrhoe, daughter of Achelous, spelled differently; the Callirrhoe link already covers her.

Atlas is father of a different Hesperus (the Hesperid-related, Atlantid Hesperus/Hesperis tradition); Argonautica's Hesperus is Eos's son, and the editor ruled Atlas parent of Lucifer wrong everywhere.
Aegle the Hesperid is daughter of Hesperus son of Atlas (or Nyx/Erebus), a different Hesperus from the Evening Star son of Eos.
Ovid's Metamorphoses makes Ceyx son of Lucifer (the Morning Star), not Hesperus the Evening Star; the editor's rule on Lucifer shows the confusion.
Neptune's mother is Rhea/Ops; Cybele is a conflation, and no source in the book supports her as his mother.
Duplicate of Ancaeus spelled differently; it is the same person, so the duplicate should be merged, not kept.
Nireus is the son of Charopus and Aglaia, not Poseidon, in the Iliad.
Eryx is son of Aphrodite and Butes (or Poseidon in some versions); the Neptune link is unsupported here.
The Doliones are a people, a group taken for a person.
The Moliones are a pair of brothers treated as one person; they are sons of Molione, and Poseidon is claimed as their father in some accounts. Not a single person.
Kleatos is a Molione brother, not a distinct child of Poseidon; the link duplicates the Moliones.
Despoina is a cult title of Persephone, taken for a person; Pausanias says Demeter bore her to Poseidon.
In Aeschylus' Persians, Darius is the husband of Atossa and father of Xerxes, so the link is reversed. Wikidata's Xerxes I as father belongs to Darius, the crown prince, a different person.
Theseus abducted Helen as a girl (Pausanias) but the union was not a marriage; the editor reads non-marriage spouse links as lovers.
Paris carried Helen off while she was still Menelaus' wife, so the Iliad treats her as his lover, not a lawful wife.
Pasithea is the wife of Hypnos (Sleep) in Iliad 14 (Hera promises her to him) and in Wikipedia and Wikidata; she was not merely a lover.
In the Odyssey, Orsilochus son of Idomeneus is a Cretan whom Odysseus claims to have killed. That is a different figure from this tree's Idomeneus, and the Hesiod text names no son for him.
Pausanias makes Tritea the daughter of Triton (the sea god), so it belongs to Triton, not Phorcys.
Aegle was a lover for whom Theseus abandoned Ariadne (Hesiod via Plutarch), not a wife.
Duplicate spelling of Demophon, son of Theseus; the fall-of-troy spelling is the same person and should be merged with Demophon.
Hippolyta is the Amazon queen, a consort and not a wedded wife in the editor's rule; same figure as Antiope in some accounts.

link: Theseus parent_of Iphigenia, daughter of Theseus
reasons: Pausanias mentions Iphigenia as daughter of Theseus and Helen by one tradition, but she is not Agamemnon's Iphigenia; keep separate from the famous Iphigenia.

link: Theseus parent_of Melanippus, son of Theseus
reasons: Melanippus is a different person; the attribution to Theseus is unsupported.
Alcmena married Rhadamanthys in Boeotia after Amphitryon's death (Apollodorus; Pherecydes; Plutarch); it was a marriage, though listed under a spouse link from another book, so keep it as spouse.

In Virgil (Aeneid) and Ovid, Picus is the son of Saturn, the Roman god. That is not the Greek Cronus's son in this tradition and was merged through the Saturn/Cronus identification, so it is not supported for Aeschylus.
Sicinus is the son of Thoas by the Naiad Oenoe (Oenoe's son), but in Apollodorus Sicinus is not Thoas' child; the link comes from Argonautica, not this book's tradition.
Hesiod makes Aegle Theseus's lover, for whom he abandoned Ariadne; not a marriage.
Tradition (Pausanias, Plutarch) has Antiope bear Hippolytus to Theseus; Wikidata lists her as spouse. Sources differ, so the lover link is not clearly wrong.
Statius treats Hippolyte as Theseus's wife, same Amazon as Antiope/Hippolyta in other versions; link fine, but should be merged with Antiope.

link: Theseus parent_of Iphigenia, daughter of Theseus
reasons: Pausanias says this Iphigenia was Helen's daughter by Theseus, raised by Clytemnestra; she is not the daughter of Agamemnon, so a link to Theseus must not be confused with her.

link: Theseus parent_of Melanippus, son of Theseus
reasons: Unsupported; Melanippus is not a recognized son of Theseus in the sources.
This is a placeholder, not a named person. Pausanias gives no son of Crius here, and Apollodorus names Astraeus, Pallas and Perses as his sons by Eurybia.
Per the Catalogue of Women and Wikidata, Polycaste, daughter of Nestor, married Telemachus; Pausanias gives no contrary tradition.

Telegonus tradition (Eugammon, Hesiod's Theogony ending) has Telemachus marry Circe, but the editor's rule reads non-marriage spouse links as lovers; Pausanias does not tell this, so keep it as lover only.
Thestius, father of Leda and Althaea, is son of Ares only in a rare tradition; Apollodorus gives Agenor and Demonice as parents (Demonice was Ares' daughter, not the mother).
Tmolus son of Ares and Theogone is a different figure from the Lydian mountain god in Ovid.
Harmonia is a daughter of Mars and Venus, but the label 'Cadmus's wife' duplicates the Harmonia node and is not a person.
Harmonia is Mars's daughter (with Venus), not his spouse; she married Cadmus.
Duplicate of Penthesilea under another spelling; keep one node.
Panic is a personification, not a person; Phobos and Deimos are Ares' sons, and Panic is a collective idea.

link: Mars parent_of Melanippus, son of Ares
reasons: Descriptive title duplicating a person; the tie is unclear.
Mercury is son of Jupiter and Maia, so only a half-brother; Statius uses loose language.

In Ovid's Metamorphoses Chaos is the primal unformed mass at the start (1.5-9), with no parent. Hesiod (Theogony 116) also gives Chaos no parent. Only the Orphic Rhapsodies make Chronos his father, and the book does not follow that tradition.

Pausanias gives Oeneus a different Pandion-line parentage (the Athenian Pandion belongs to another tradition); Thebaid and Iliad make Oeneus son of Porthaon (Portheus), so Pandion is unsupported here.
Endeis, Peleus' mother, was a daughter of Chiron or Sciron, not a Nereid. She is Thetis' mother-in-law, not her sister; the link comes from a confusion in Pausanias.
Phocus was the son of Aeacus and the Nereid Psamathe, and Peleus' half-brother. He is not Thetis' child; the link confuses Psamathe with Thetis.
Glaucus loved the sea-monster Scylla (Ovid, Metamorphoses), not Nisus' daughter who betrayed Megara; Pausanias' Scylla is the Megarian princess.
Deidameia bore Neoptolemos to Achilles on Scyros, but no marriage is told; the editor's rule reads non-marriage spouse links as lover.

link: Achilles parent_of Pyrrhus, king of Epirus
reasons: Pyrrhus of Epirus was a historical king descended from Neoptolemos; he is not Achilles' son. Neoptolemos (also called Pyrrhus) is Achilles' son.
Hyrie is the mother of the other Cycnus, the son of Apollo and Hyrie, whose story Ovid tells in Book 7 (the Boeotian lake). The Cycnus who mourned Phaethon is the son of Sthenelus.
Hesiod's Homeric-style tale has Hermes loving Dryops' daughter, mother of Pan; she was not a wife. The editor reads non-marriage spouse links as lover links.
Pindar's 'Angelia' (Message) is a personification, not Fame (Pheme). Hermes' daughter here is a namesake confusion.
Eleusis as a son of Hermes is a pausanias variant; the editor limited Eleusis' parentage to Ogygus or Daira in pausanias, not Apollodorus.
Pausanias calls Idomeneus a descendant of Minos and Pasiphae, not a son. His father was Deucalion, Minos's son, so Minos is his grandfather.
Editor's rule: only marriages count as spouse; in the Odyssey Helen was Menelaus's wife, and Paris carried her off (she was his partner in Troy, not husband under the rule).
Theseus abducted Helen as a girl (Pausanias); not a marriage, so a lover per editor's rule.
Nicostratus is Menelaus's son by a slave woman (Megapenthes' brother in some accounts); the Odyssey says Helen bore only Hermione.

Hesiod's Theogony and Apollodorus treat Echidna as Typhon's mate, and Wikidata lists her as his spouse. Under the editor's rule only marriages count as spouse, and this is a mating, so lover is acceptable; keep as is.
Deidameia bore Neoptolemus to Achilles on Scyros but was not his wife in the usual tradition; the editor's rule reads non-marriage spouse links as lovers.
The Telemachus marriage is a Telegony tradition not told in Apollodorus; under the editor's rule a non-marriage spouse link is read as a lover link, and the book does not state a marriage.

Apollodorus makes Actor a different figure, the Elean Molione's father/Augeas's associate, not Augeas's brother; Augeas is son of Helios (or Phorbas, Poseidon) and Actor is not named as a sibling in any Theoi-listed source.

Pausanias's Clymenus is a Argive/Hermionean cult figure, a title of Hades, not a separate brother; in Hermione Clymenus is a name of Hades, so this is a cult title taken as a person and duplicates Aidoneus.

link: Arcas parent_of Pelasgus, son of Arcas
reasons: Pausanias makes Pelasgus the father of Lycaon and an ancestor of Arcas, not his son. The link confuses the earlier Pelasgus with a later namesake.
This is the Amazon Antiope (sister of Hippolyta), a different being from the Theban Antiope of Odyssey 11, mother of Amphion and Zethus.
Hippolyta is the sister of the Amazon Antiope, not of Asopus' daughter.
The Naiads are a group, not a single person; Ovid's Metamorphoses calls the Echinades nymphs, not Achelous's children as a group.
In the Aeneid Latinus is the son of Faunus (and Marica). Faunus is the Roman counterpart of Pan, but the tradition is separate and the two are not the same being.

link: Leonidas parent_of Cleomenes III, son of Leonidas
reasons: Pausanias names two Leonidases: Leonidas I of Thermopylae, and Leonidas II, father of Cleomenes III and Epiclidas and son of Cleonymus. Those children belong to Leonidas II.
Epiclidas was a son of Leonidas II, the Hellenistic king, not of Leonidas I.

link: Cleonymus, father of Leonidas parent_of Leonidas
reasons: Cleonymus was the father of Leonidas II, the grandfather of Cleomenes III, not of Leonidas I, whose father was Anaxandridas.
The Doliones are a people, a group taken for a person; their eponym Dolion was a different figure.
Laestrygon is the eponym of a people, and the link rests on a misread tradition in Hesiod.
Podaleirius is a son of Asclepius, not Poseidon.
Chios is an island or eponym, and no Poseidon parentage is stated in this book.
Sarpedon the Lycian is a son of Zeus; the Poseidon link is a rare namesake of the Thracian Sarpedon.
In Pausanias, Alpheus was a river-god who pursued Artemis (or Arethusa) and failed, so he was never her lover. This isn't a relationship in Aeschylus.
Pallas is a Titan son of Crius (Hesiod) or an epithet of Athena; Zeus is not his father.
Selene was confused with Diana/Pandia; Hesiod's Selene is a Titan's daughter, and the editor ruled Zeus parent of Selene wrong. Pandia is Zeus and Selene's daughter only in the Homeric Hymn.
Pandia comes from the Selene confusion, and the editor has ruled Artemis parent of Pandia wrong.
A group taken for a person; the Graces are already listed individually as Aglaea, Euphrosyne and Thalia.
A group; the Muses are already listed individually.
A group, not a person.
Opportunity (Kairos) is an abstraction in Pausanias, and Zeus is not named as his father.
The Sibyl is called daughter of Zeus and Lamia only in Pausanias; here it is a cross-book link, and Zeus is not her parent in this book.
Truth is a personified abstraction in Pindar, not a daughter of Zeus here.
Apollodorus lists Justice among the Seasons, whom Zeus fathered with Themis; the link duplicates this as a separate person.
Iarbas is a son of Jupiter Ammon in Virgil, a different cult figure; this is a namesake.
Erato is a Muse; Zeus's paternity of the Muses is shown separately.
Macedon is Zeus's son only in Hesiod's catalogue, not in Apollodorus.
A cult-linked figure from Pausanias, not in Apollodorus; low confidence.
Arcesius is a son of Zeus in Ovid, but Apollodorus calls him a son of Cephalus.
Megarus is a son of Zeus only in Pausanias, not in Apollodorus.
Macar is a son of Aeolus in Apollodorus, with no father link to Zeus.
Ate is the personification of delusion, from other books only.
Eris is the personification of strife, from other books only; Hesiod makes her a daughter of Night.

link: Hiero son of Hierocles parent_of Gelon
reasons: Pausanias mentions a later Gelon, son of Hiero II of Syracuse, who married Nereis daughter of Pyrrhus. The links to Hiero son of Hierocles as parent and to Nereis belong to this later Gelon, not Gelon son of Deinomenes.
Nereis married Gelon the son of Hiero II, a different man from the tyrant Gelon son of Deinomenes (brother of Hiero I).
Pausanias does not make Laius the Sphinx's father; Statius's Sphinx is a monster of Hera/Typhon-Echidna lineage, and Laius's only child here is Oedipus.
Metra is the wife of Erysichthon in Ovid's Metamorphoses (Mestra); she is not Autolycus's wife. Ovid mentions Autolycus only as the son of Mercury and Chione, and Mestra's father is Erysichthon.
Neaera is not an established wife of Autolycus; his wife is Amphithea, mother of Anticlea (Odyssey 19). Neaera in Pausanias is a different woman.
Hemithea and Tennes are children of the Trojan Cycnus (Poseidon's son), per Pausanias, not Ares' son.
Tennes is the son of the Trojan Cycnus, not of Ares' son in Hesiod.
Phylonome is the wife of the Trojan Cycnus, son of Poseidon, not of Ares' son.

Themistinoe is Ceyx's daughter, and the Shield passage addresses Cycnus as Ceyx's son-in-law, but the sentence is Heracles' speech to Iolaus, the 'you' being the charioteer Iolaus. It does not say Cycnus is Themistinoe's husband; Iolaus is.
Harmonia was Ares' lover (Aphrodite's daughter by Ares, married to Cadmus), not his wife; the editor's rule treats non-listed marriages as lovers.
Statius calls them as fellow gods only; Hermes is son of Zeus and Maia, so he is a half-brother at most, not a full sibling; unsupported sibling link.
Parthenopaeus is the son of Atalanta by Melanion or Meleager; Ares is not his father in the main tradition.

link: Heracles parent_of Hercules' sons by Megara
reasons: A group of children treated as one person; the sons by Megara should be individual nodes.
Chromis in Statius' Thebaid is a different Chromis, not a son of Heracles.
Latinus is son of Faunus the Italian king (son of Picus) in Aeneid and Metamorphoses, not Pan/Faunus of Statius's Arcadian god.
Silenus as son of Pan is a minor variant, but Statius's Faunus is Arcadian Pan; Silenus is usually a follower of Dionysus, so this link is an unsupported guess.
Ovid's Faunus is the Italian god, father of Acis in Metamorphoses; this is not Statius's Pan, though the Wikidata entry merges both.

The passage is the Homeric Hymn/Hesiod-style fragment on Nireus and Telephus or other heroes; the 'Earth-Shaker' father of both gifts does not make Poseidon Machaon's father. Machaon's father is Asclepius (Iliad 2.731; Theoi), and the sentence names a different pair.

Pasithea is a Grace/Sleep's wife in Iliad 14 (given by Hera as bride to Hypnos), not Hera's daughter; the editor ruled Pasithea parentage against Jove and Bromius, and Apollodorus does not name her as Hera's child.
Corybas is a Corybantes figure, a group/attendant tradition (often son of Cybele/Rhea-Cybele); conflates Rhea with Cybele and is unsupported here.
Editor's rule: only marriages count as spouse links. Glauce (Creusa) was Jason's betrothed or second wife, but she is not the wife Hesiod names (Medea), so she is read as a lover.
This is a group, not a person. The sons (Mermerus and Pheres) are named individually elsewhere, and Hesiod names only Medeus.

In the Odyssey (13.260) Orsilochus is a son of Idomeneus only in the invented Cretan tale, where Odysseus claims to have killed him. Apollodorus has no such son, and the Odyssey's Orsilochus is a fictional character, so this is not a real child of Idomeneus.
Clytus and Butes are sons of the Giant/Athenian Pallas (Metamorphoses, Pallas of the Pallantids), not of Athena's friend or Tritonia.
Butes is a child of a different Pallas (Metamorphoses); the Thebaid's Pallas is Athena (Tritonia).
